## Running the application {#running-app}

### Q: The application will not open (macOS "cannot be verified" / Windows "blocked") {#wont-open}

**A:** The executables are unsigned, so the operating system shows a one-time security prompt on first
launch — this is not a fault. Clear it separately for **both** MRMhub and MRMhub-viz, and again after
each update. Antivirus or endpoint-protection software may also quarantine the unsigned executable;
allow-list it if the file will not launch. See
[clearing the security prompt](setup.qmd#clearing-the-first-launch-security-prompt).

The macOS build is Apple silicon only and will not run on an Intel Mac.

### Q: MRMhub closes on start — the console opens, then returns to the shell prompt {#crash-start}

**A:** The usual cause is a malformed input file: the console opens, the application exits without
showing the menu, and the shell prompt (`$`) becomes active again — often **without a clear error
message**. Check that:

- `param.txt` is in the same folder as the executable;
- the input-file and mzML paths in `param.txt` are correct (no typos);
- no parameter name or value has a typo or wrong format;
- no input file is empty or truncated.

If in doubt, start again from the release templates. See [Input Files](input-files.qmd).

### Q: The application is slow or runs out of memory {#system-req}

**A:** Integration is multithreaded, controlled by `num_threads` in `param.txt` — this affects speed
only, never the results:

- **Keep multithreading active.** Ensure `num_threads` is greater than `1` (the template default is
  `2`); `1` runs single-threaded and is slowest. Raising it toward the CPU's core count speeds up the
  integration.
- **Do not exceed the core count.** Setting more threads than the machine has cores does **not** cause
  an error, but the extra threads only oversubscribe the CPU and add context-switching overhead — no
  faster, sometimes slower.
- **Leave a few cores free if you need the machine.** Assigning every core makes the whole computer
  unresponsive during processing; leave 1–2 for the operating system (e.g. set `6` on an 8-core CPU).

For memory, allow **16 GB RAM** for large sequences (8 GB minimum) and ample disk space for the
`misc/` folder, tables, and PDFs. If the application will not start **at all**, see
[The application will not open](#wont-open) instead. See [Installation](setup.qmd) and
[Input Files](input-files.qmd).

## Input data and files {#input-files}

### Q: The mzML files are misread, or conversion fails {#msconvert-settings}

**A:** Convert with a **recent** ProteoWizard MSConvert (Windows only), using **mzML** output,
**32-bit** encoding, and **Write index** enabled. For SCIEX data, keep the `.wiff` and `.wiff.scan`
files in the same folder. See [mzML Conversion](msconvert.qmd).

### Q: After editing a CSV, integration results are incorrect or implausible {#csv-misread}

**A:** Columns are matched by **header name**, so a renamed or misspelled required column stops the run
with an explicit error rather than being silently misread (see
[the "column not found" error](#col-not-found)). Plausible-but-wrong results instead come from
spreadsheet editors corrupting the cell **values**: dropped leading zeros, values like `16:0` coerced
to dates (format the cells as text), a semicolon delimiter from a non-English locale, a UTF-8
byte-order mark that breaks the first header, and stray trailing spaces or blank rows. File names must
also match the mzML files exactly (`.mzML` extension, correct case). When results look wrong, reopen
the CSV in a plain-text editor and compare the values against the template.

### Q: INTEGRATOR reports a "column not found" error {#col-not-found}

**A:** `run_order.csv` and `feature_list.csv` are read by matching the **header row**, so a required
column whose name INTEGRATOR cannot find stops the run with a `<name> column not found!` message. The
usual causes are a misspelled or renamed header, a deleted column, or a stray space inserted **inside**
a name (`Feature ID` is read as `Feature` and no longer matches `Feature_ID`). Column *order* does not
matter. Restore the exact header names from the [templates](https://github.com/SLINGhub/MRMhub/releases)
— the required names are listed in [Input Files](input-files.qmd#sample-list-run_order.csv) (matching
is case-insensitive).

### Q: Which input files are required, and can they be renamed? {#file-names}

**A:** Only `param.txt` has a fixed name and must sit beside the executable. The sample and feature
lists may be renamed via the `batch_info` and `transition_list` entries in `param.txt`. See
[Input Files](input-files.qmd).

### Q: A per-feature peak-width override has no effect {#peakwidth-brackets}

**A:** The global `peak_width` in `param.txt` uses brackets — `[w, x, y, z]` — but the per-feature
override in the feature list is entered **without** brackets, as `w, x, y, z`. Brackets, or the wrong
number of values, cause it to be ignored. See [Tuning Peak Integration](tuning.qmd).

### Q: RT-shift correction seems inactive {#rtshift-zero}

**A:** `RT_shift = [0.0, 0.0]` disables it. The lower bound is negative (earlier), the upper positive
(later), e.g. `[-0.2, 0.2]`; a small non-zero window is recommended even for stable methods. See
[Tuning Peak Integration](tuning.qmd).

## Transition matching and validation (Step 1) {#matching}

### Q: Validation finished but wrote no report files {#no-report}

**A:** No report is the expected result of a **clean** validation. The `missing_*.txt` files are
written **only when problems are found**, so their absence confirms that every mzML file and transition
matched, and the run can proceed. See [Processing Workflow](running.qmd#step-1-data-validation).

### Q: What do the missing_*.txt reports mean? {#missing-files}

**A:** They are written only on problems: **missing_files.txt** (mzML listed but absent, or present
but unlisted), **missing_compounds.txt** (transitions not matched in the mzML), and
**missing_details.txt** (which samples lack a given transition). The analysis may still proceed. See
[Processing Workflow](running.qmd#step-1-data-validation).

### Q: A transition I defined never appears in the results {#no-match}

**A:** Locate the cause by step:

- **Not matched (Step 1)** — if it is listed in `missing_compounds.txt`, it was not found in the mzML
  data. Matching is by precursor and product *m/z* and RT, within `mz_tol` and `RT_tol`; check the
  transition-list values against the mzML and widen `mz_tol` if the *m/z* calibration is slightly off.
- **Matched but not integrated (Step 3)** — the transition is present but no peak was found, so its
  area is zero and its `long.csv` fields are empty (see [area reported as zero](#area-zero)).
- **No plot produced (Step 4)** — the transition has data but no PDF (see
  [a feature has no PDF](#pdf-missing)).

### Q: Why was a transition dropped from every sample? {#dropped-all}

**A:** **Current limitation** — INTEGRATOR integrates only transitions present in **all** mzML files;
one missing from a single file is dropped for the whole dataset (reported in the missing_*.txt files).
Acquire it in every sample, or exclude the files that lack it. See
[Processing Workflow](running.qmd#step-1-data-validation).

### Q: The same transition appears more than once in an mzML file {#duplicate-transition}

**A:** When a transition with near-identical Q1/Q3 and MRM windows occurs several times, INTEGRATOR
prompts for the MRM index; the `chromatogram index` column in the feature list can also fix the
assignment.

## Peak detection and integration (Steps 2–3) {#integration}

### Q: A feature's area is reported as zero {#area-zero}

**A:** No peak was found within `RT_tol` of the expected RT — the same reason measurement cells are
left empty in `long.csv`. Check the expected RT, confirm the *m/z* match, and widen `RT_tol` for
drifting peaks. See [Tuning Peak Integration](tuning.qmd).

### Q: A wrong or adjacent peak is integrated {#wrong-peak}

**A:** Usually `RT_tol` or `peak_width` is too wide, or the expected RT is off, so a neighbouring peak
falls inside the window. Narrow the window, or set a per-feature width or fixed bounds for that feature
— confirm the effect in [MRMhub-viz](viz.qmd) first. See [Tuning Peak Integration](tuning.qmd).

### Q: A partially overlapping peak is not integrated correctly {#overlap}

**A:** Partially resolved peaks often cannot be separated by the window alone: adjust `peak_width` and
the integration bounds, or set fixed per-feature borders as a last resort. Fully co-eluting analytes
(identical RT) cannot be separated at all and require a chromatographic or MRM-transition change. See
[Tuning Peak Integration](tuning.qmd).

### Q: Retention-time drift is not tracked across the sequence {#drift-untracked}

**A:** Choose reference samples from **early** in the sequence, mutually well aligned, and set
`RT_shift` / `RT_shift_bound` to cover the real drift. See [Tuning Peak Integration](tuning.qmd).

### Q: I set a uniform width for a feature, but its borders still shift across samples {#uniform-wobble}

**A:** This is expected. `uniform_width` fixes the borders on the **RT-drift-corrected** scale, where
they are identical across samples. In **absolute** RT — as plotted in the PDFs — they move with each
sample's RT shift, so they appear to wobble. See [Tuning Peak Integration](tuning.qmd).

## Re-running after edits {#rerun}

### Q: A changed parameter has no effect on the integration {#no-effect}

**A:** Work through the likely causes:

- **The steps were not re-run** — an edit to any input file takes effect only after re-running from
  **Step 1**; a change to the plots needs **Step 4** re-run.
- **The value is in the wrong format** — check brackets, commas, and sign (see the
  [peak-width](#peakwidth-brackets) and [RT-shift](#rtshift-zero) notes).
- **The change is too small** to alter the result — try a larger adjustment.
- **A required column header is misspelled or missing**, so the edited value never reaches INTEGRATOR
  (this now stops the run — see [the "column not found" error](#col-not-found)).

### Q: I edited an input file — what must be re-run? {#what-to-rerun}

**A:** Any input-file edit means restarting from **Step 1**. Editing only `RT_matrix.csv` (manual
borders) means re-running **Step 3** alone. See [Processing Workflow](running.qmd).

### Q: My manual RT_matrix.csv edits disappeared {#rtmatrix-lost}

**A:** Re-running **Step 2** overwrites `RT_matrix.csv`. Make manual edits only once integration is
otherwise final, back up the file, and re-run **Step 3 alone**. See
[Tuning Peak Integration](tuning.qmd).

## Results: viewing and output files {#results}

### Q: MRMhub-viz shows nothing, or will not load a dataset {#viz-empty}

**A:** MRMhub-viz reads the `misc/` folder, so Step 3 (peak integration) must have run at least once
and `misc/` must exist; the viz executable must also sit in the same folder as MRMhub. If `misc/` was
deleted, re-run Step 3. See [MRMhub-viz](viz.qmd).

### Q: PDF generation (Step 4) produces no plots, or plotting fails {#pdf-fail}

**A:** PDF plotting is carried out by the bundled R script, so it needs a working **R installation**.
Check, in order:

- **R is installed** — install it from [CRAN](https://cran.r-project.org/) (no additional R packages
  are required).
- **R is on the system `PATH`** — the executable calls R from the command line, so `Rscript` must be
  resolvable in a terminal (verify with `Rscript --version`). On Windows the installer does not add R
  to the `PATH` automatically; add R's `bin` directory manually (see the CRAN R-for-Windows FAQ, §2.29
  *"Rcmd is not found in my PATH!"*, at <https://cran.r-project.org/bin/windows/base/rw-FAQ.html>).
- **The plotting script is present** — `MRMhub_plot.r` must be in the project folder; use the copy
  bundled in the release.
- **The `misc/` folder exists** — it is produced by Step 3 and is required for plotting.

Plotting can also be slow for large projects. See [Installation](setup.qmd).

### Q: A feature has no PDF, or its PDF is in the low-intensity folder {#pdf-missing}

**A:** A transition gets **no PDF** if it is not defined or not matched in `feature_list.csv`, or not
present in **all** mzML files (see [dropped from every sample](#dropped-all)). If a peak is missing or
its area falls below the intensity threshold, the plot is written to `by_transition_low/` instead of
`by_transition/`.

### Q: A transition's PDF is in the low-intensity folder but should not be {#pdf-low-wrong}

**A:** `by_transition_low/` holds transitions whose integrated area is below the threshold, so a real
peak landing there usually means it was not detected, the expected RT is off, or the integration
parameters are unsuitable — i.e. the wrong peak (or none) was integrated. See
[a wrong peak is integrated](#wrong-peak) and [Tuning Peak Integration](tuning.qmd).

### Q: The RT values in quant_raw.csv do not match the peak apex {#quant-rt}

**A:** The `RT` row in `quant_raw.csv` is the **expected** RT from the feature list, not the measured
apex, and the file holds **areas only**. Apex RT, height, and FWHM are in `long.csv`. See
[Output Files](output-files.qmd).
